body:
Custom rules previously left native AIs planning disabled training, waiting for unattainable levels, and investing in starvation recovery or combat that could not work. Controllers now read the effective match rules before selecting construction, prerequisites, budgets, staffing and attack work. Default tuning is retained.

“No upgrades” now disables both unit training and building upgrades. Repairs, healing, swarm production, starting unit levels and existing higher-level buildings remain available. The stable `unitTraining` rule id and save compatibility floor are preserved. Restored training visits and obsolete saved AI queues are handled without adding serialized fields.

JavaScript controllers can read the additive, read-only `game.rules()` snapshot; the shipped example adapts training staffing. Structured headless games accept repeatable `--rule name=value`, tournament jobs accept `config.rules`, loaded-save overrides are rejected, and effective settings are recorded in results.

Engine fixes:
- Authoritative construction and script validation reject healthy-building upgrades when disabled, while permitting repairs.
- Units cannot select training visits when disabled; restored visits cancel or exit without gains. Saved hungry units do not keep seeking food under no hunger.
- Farms with regrowth disabled can harvest their final finite wheat seed.
- Touch repair/upgrade controls use effective fortress HP.

Review improvement: Cabino migrates older saved warrior reservation counters and usage indexes to the recruitment bucket used when training is disabled. Without migrating both, releasing a saved claim could wrap an unsigned count and withhold the army. A dedicated regression checks migration, safe release and unchanged default loads. Consequential planning gates now explain their failed assumptions in code; the custom-game, JavaScript, headless, Maxima and tournament guides are updated.

Legacy forbidden farming paint has no owner metadata, so it is preserved on load rather than clearing potentially player-owned restrictions. New growth-dependent planning is gated.

`SIM_REVISION` increases from 11 to 12. Saves retain their format and compatibility floor. Simulation changes can affect earlier custom-rule replay outcomes; online matches and verifiers are separated by the simulation key.

Validation: fresh-game qualification on `39bab83c9`, then final review checks on `77b62164c`:

- 144 native matches and 18 JavaScript smoke matches across nine profiles, fixed seeds, swapped seats, two established maps and a 30,000-tick cap: no crashes, no live rule-selection violations, no disabled training visits. All controllers emitted work. The plan omitted Maxima from its inventory; all eight native AIs are covered.
- Final review: 92 relevant Linux engine cases and 87 relevant macOS engine cases, plus 25 real-binary CLI cases on each platform. The earlier qualification also passed 18 farm cases. Coverage includes save/load continuation, historical saves, queued work, disabled planning, repairs, JavaScript profiles, replay/network acceptance and touch controls.
- All 16 default games match the pre-change revision's detailed tick traces (359,914 ticks). All 24 affected macOS/Linux scenarios produce identical complete checksum files (4,096 ticks each), refreshed on the final review revision.
- Python tournament adapter: 25 cases. Translation and simulation-version/golden checks pass. Two new strings remain pending in non-English catalogs.

[Review evidence and reproduction commands](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/ai-rule-evidence-678) include every qualification save, replay, telemetry log, settings and result; selected full checksum traces, cross-platform pairs and complete trace hashes are published. Full tournament traces are retained in the Linux validation directory.

The full hosted matrix, Windows, Android and browser equivalence were not run. Current master (`b1a8603b`, language/font and display fixes) merges cleanly. Final merged-source integration validation is recorded in the verification comment. A prior Xvfb resize failure passed on retry and in final validation.

Gameplay effect: custom variants change investment and recruitment to avoid unavailable mechanics; they do not optimize variant strategy or add victory strategies. Peaceful conquest-only games may remain unresolved. No human playthrough is claimed; custom-rule pacing and feel remain unverified. The author requested merge after code review and automated verification.

comments.body:
Local/VM verification for `39bab83c967239e38e1310f12650c988501831fd`, based on `69db1fb5d`.

[Accessible evidence, commands, manifests and limitations](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/ai-rule-evidence-678).

Environment: Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 / Apple Clang 21.0.0; Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 7.0 x86_64 / GCC 13.3.0. Repository-pinned SDL configuration 11: SDL 3.4.16, image 3.4.6, ttf 3.2.2, net 3.2.0, WebP 1.6.0; exact manifest hashes and compiler/link flags are in the evidence. Native `release=1` builds used `GLOB2_SDL3_PREFIX=<pinned-prefix> scons release=1 -j8 engine-tests <build-dir>/src/glob2` (macOS `-j6`). Every qualification game used `--compute-threads 1 --compute-experiments none` and `GLOB2_TEST_AI_RULE_AUDIT=1`.

Results:

- 144 native and 18 JavaScript games, nine profiles, swapped seats, fixed seeds, alternating `SmallForTwo.map.gz` and `balanced_for_2.map.gz`, 30,000-tick cap. All 162 runs and replay audits pass; 3,653,518 ticks total. Every controller emitted work; disabled training visits remain zero. Exact per-game commands/settings/results, all initial/final saves, replays and telemetry are in `qualification/`; `qualification-analysis.json` records the checks.
- Linux: 91 focused engine cases plus 18 `FarmAreas` cases and 25 real-binary CLI cases pass. macOS: 82 engine and 25 CLI cases pass. Exact suite filters are in the evidence README. Coverage includes all controllers, saved queues and worker assignments, training/upgrade authority, repairs, feeding versus healing/production, historical saves, JavaScript profiles, replay boundaries, relay verification, and touch actions. Linux touch checks used Xvfb.
- All 16 default games match pre-change `79229b3101c6bd6e0c83abb5ed55579834595785` at every tick: 359,914 detailed tick records, no differences. Full baseline/candidate traces for one 30,000-tick match are published; complete comparison results are in `logs/default-comparison.json`.
- 24 loaded scenarios spanning all eight native AIs and six affected profiles match on macOS and Linux at every tick. Both platforms' complete 4,096-tick trace files, initial/final saves and binary/trace hashes are published in `cross-mac/`, `cross-linux/` and `cross-comparison.json`.
- `python3 test/test_tournaments.py`: 25 pass. Translation checks and `python3 test/check_sim_revision.py --base 69db1fb5d` pass. `SIM_REVISION=12`; golden record/trace regenerated together; save format and compatibility floor preserved.

Integration: fetched current master before final review. `429f505684338b5676356e5f32817d4f8f362db3` adds language/font handling. `git merge-tree` reports no conflicts (tree `6a3bd55513f4bb029af1eceb3060078d287ebd31`). Overlaying its merged changed files on Linux builds successfully and passes nine AIRules cases plus golden verification. Its source provenance and logs are published. The feature branch stays on its reviewed base because the newer work does not alter simulation.

Limits: the full hosted matrix, Windows, Android and browser equivalence were not run. Full tournament checksum files are retained in the Linux qualification directory; their hashes are published along with representative full traces. An earlier Xvfb resize timeout passed on retry and in final validation. An initially missed copy of the regenerated golden trace was corrected; both resolved failures are retained. Qualification is evidence of legal decisions and continued activity, not variant optimization or proof against every possible stall. Bounded peaceful/conquest-only or immortal-combat matches may remain unresolved.

The broader “No upgrades” meaning and individual engine fixes are documented in the PR and custom-game guide. Default tick traces remain identical. A maintainer playthrough is still needed to judge custom-rule pacing and feel; the PR remains draft for that review.

Final review verification for `77b62164c16705927052a165cdfd7d5afcccf377`, base `69db1fb5d`.

[Published review evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/ai-rule-evidence-678/review), [environment, commands and limits](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/codex/ai-rule-evidence-678/README.md).

The requested sub-agent reviewed the PR, improved consequential AI comments and documentation, and fixed Cabino legacy warrior reservation migration. A saved high-level reservation could otherwise be released against an unsigned zero in the base bucket, withholding the army. The added test covers default-load preservation, requested/reserved/used counters, usage indexes and safe release. The sub-agent reviewed the migration and regression again with no actionable findings.

Final native release builds use the same Apple Clang 21/macOS arm64 and GCC 13.3/Ubuntu x86_64 toolchains and pinned SDL configuration 11 recorded above. Commands are the evidence README's focused engine filters, CLI integration, cross.py, tournament unit tests and sim-revision contract. macOS passed 87 engine cases; Linux passed 92 including Xvfb touch checks. Both passed 25 real-binary CLI cases. All 24 refreshed loaded scenarios match complete per-tick checksums across platforms (4,096 ticks each). Both JavaScript profiles enforce read-only snapshots. Python tournament tests (25) and sim/golden contract pass.

Fresh-game qualification remains the recorded 144 native + 18 JavaScript games: the only new behavior change is Cabino load migration. Default preservation is covered by the existing 359,914-tick baseline comparison and the new default-load regression. Final traces, saves, replays, settings, binary/input/trace hashes and logs are published as review archives. The regression's first compile used an incorrect fixture constructor; corrected before these passes, with failure logs retained.

Fetched current master `b1a8603bedf079e587307c77b665e3090bd2d2e5`. It merges without conflicts (tree `678fdf08baf2e7e9cbdfbfb5c8e07caa8271ae97`). Its merged-source overlay builds on Linux and passes 11 cases: all AIRules tests plus the committed golden-record verifier. Exact paths/provenance and logs are published. No rebase was needed.

Full hosted CI, Windows, Android and browser simulation equivalence remain unverified. Old forbidden-area paint lacks ownership metadata and is preserved to avoid clearing player restrictions. No human playthrough is claimed; custom-rule pacing and feel remain unverified. The author explicitly requested merge following code review and validation.

title: Make native and JavaScript AIs respect custom game rules
